evidence.title: Fictional 360 feedback summary — Sophie Bennett
evidence.purpose: Support development planning after recent peer and stakeholder feedback.
evidence.sourceSummary: Reviewed fictional 360 summary highlighting clearer expectations with former peers and remaining unevenness in difficult performance conversations.

observations.title: Clearer expectations with former peers
observations.description: Stakeholders describe more consistent expectation-setting in team huddles over the last quarter.
observations.behaviouralEvidence: Peers noted that weekly priorities are now stated explicitly rather than assumed.
observations.developmentImplication: Continue reinforcing expectation-setting when standards slip.

observations.title: Uneven confidence in performance conversations
observations.description: Feedback suggests progress conversations still feel delayed when the issue is interpersonal rather than operational.
observations.behaviouralEvidence: Two reviewers noted delayed follow-up after informal concerns were raised.
observations.developmentImplication: Useful next focus: rehearse earlier, shorter performance conversations.

developmentSignals: Earlier performance conversations when concerns emerge
limitations: This is a fictionalised 360 summary for demonstration. It is not a proprietary assessment report.

evidence.title: Fictional DISC preference summary — Marcus Reed
evidence.purpose: Provide contextual preference evidence alongside manager reflection.
evidence.sourceSummary: The DISC-style summary suggests a preference for direct, fast-paced decision making under operational pressure.

observations.title: Preference for pace and directness
observations.description: The DISC report suggests a preference for direct, fast-paced decision making. Recent development conversations provide some supporting evidence, particularly under operational pressure.
observations.behaviouralEvidence: Manager notes describe rapid triage during warehouse disruptions.
observations.developmentImplication: Explore how pace supports delivery without crowding out supervisor development time.
observations.assessmentContext: Preference evidence only — not a measure of ability or promotion suitability.
observations.limitations: Assessment describes preferences or reported patterns, not proven capability.

developmentSignals: Protect strategic and developmental capacity from constant firefighting
contradictoryEvidence: The assessment suggests a strong preference for rapid action, while recent conversations describe reduced capacity for longer-term planning. The available evidence does not establish why these differ.
limitations: Fictionalised preference summary for demonstration. Not a proprietary DISC report.

evidence.title: Manager reflection — protecting strategic capacity
evidence.purpose: Capture observed behaviour after recent operations pressure.
evidence.sourceSummary: Manager reflection notes improving supervisor ownership in one area, with strategic capacity still crowded by escalation habits.

observations.title: Supervisor ownership emerging
observations.description: One supervisor now resolves routine escalations before involving Marcus.
observations.behaviouralEvidence: Two consecutive weeks without unnecessary evening escalations from that supervisor.
observations.developmentImplication: Test the same ownership pattern with a second supervisor.

developmentSignals: Reduce personal involvement in routine escalations
limitations: Single manager reflection — broaden with further observed examples.
